name: Formulation of scientific questions and hypotheses

questions.q: What is the first step in the scientific method?
A hypothesis is best described as:
Which of the following is a testable scientific question?
a: Which plant fertilizer increases growth the most?
What is the best color for a lab coat?

questions.q: What is the standard format for a scientific hypothesis?
Why must a hypothesis be testable?
a: So you can prove it is true
So you can perform an experiment to gather evidence
Because it is a rule of nature
To make it harder for students

questions.q: If you are testing how light affects plant growth, what is a valid hypothesis?
a: If plants receive more light, then they will grow taller.
Light is a type of energy.

questions.q: What do you do if your experiment shows your hypothesis was incorrect?
a: Change the data to match the hypothesis
Accept the findings and revise your hypothesis

questions.q: Which of these is a key characteristic of a good scientific question?
a: It has a 'yes' or 'no' answer only.
It can be answered by an experiment or investigation.
It is a matter of personal opinion.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'because' part in a hypothesis?
a: To provide a scientific reason for the prediction

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a good scientific question?
a: How does temperature affect the rate of decay?
How many ants can fit in a box?
Why is the grass green (a matter of value judgment rather than testability)?
Does water speed affect soil erosion?

questions.q: What should be avoided when forming a hypothesis?
In the statement 'If I increase the water, then the plant will grow more', what is the prediction?
Before forming a hypothesis, what should you do?
a: Conduct background research on the topic

questions.q: A well-formulated hypothesis connects the:
Which of these is an example of a research-based question?
a: How does salinity affect the hatching rate of brine shrimp?

questions.q: What makes a hypothesis 'testable'?
a: You can measure the variables involved.

questions.q: If your hypothesis is 'If I use more sugar, then the yeast will produce more gas', what is the independent variable?
Which of these is the 'If' part of a hypothesis?
Why is it important for a hypothesis to be falsifiable?
a: So it can potentially be proven wrong by evidence
To make it harder to guess
To ensure it is never tested

questions.q: What is the main goal of a scientific experiment?
a: To gather data to support or reject a hypothesis

questions.q: Which word is usually found in a well-written hypothesis?
How does background knowledge help you form a hypothesis?
a: It allows you to make an educated prediction
It tells you the answer before you start
It is not helpful at all

questions.q: What is the difference between a question and a hypothesis?
a: A question is the problem; a hypothesis is the proposed answer
A hypothesis is the problem; a question is the answer
A question is always long; a hypothesis is always short

questions.q: When writing a hypothesis, you should:
Why is 'because' vital in a hypothesis?
a: It links the prediction to biological principles

questions.q: Which variable is included in the 'then' part of the hypothesis?
What is a scientific investigation?
a: A process of asking and answering questions through testing

questions.q: What does a hypothesis allow a scientist to do?
What is wrong with the hypothesis: 'If I run fast, then I will feel better'?
a: 'Feel better' is subjective and hard to measure

questions.q: How should a hypothesis be treated?
What happens if evidence contradicts your hypothesis?
a: You must reject or modify the hypothesis
You must continue until it works

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid biological question?
a: Does music increase the growth rate of beans?
Is music the best form of entertainment?

questions.q: Which part of a hypothesis indicates the independent variable?
Why do scientists share their hypotheses?
a: To let others test them or refine them

questions.q: What is an 'educated' prediction?
a: A guess based on prior knowledge or research

questions.q: In 'If temperature rises, then enzyme activity will increase because particles move faster', what is the reasoning?
What should you check before finalizing your scientific question?
Why is it important to clearly state the independent variable in your hypothesis?
a: To know what factor is being manipulated

questions.q: A hypothesis is never described as 'proven' because:
a: Science is always open to new evidence

questions.q: How does a hypothesis make an experiment 'fair'?
a: It helps define the variables that must be controlled
